subject: AtlasGrid: Optimize Toolkit pilot — packaging, batching/cache guidance & quantization options
messages:
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@atlasgrid.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T09:12:00-07:00
To: sofia_ivanova
Subject: Quick question on Optimize Toolkit pilot structure

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. AtlasGrid is keen to run a small pilot of Redwood's Optimize Toolkit (we want to test batching + KV caching and a quantized runtime path for our high-throughput document summarization pipeline). A couple of asks from our side before procurement engages:

- High-level pricing for a 3-month pilot (est. 50M tokens/month), including any one-off credits or onboarding waivers.
- Technical guidance: which quantization profiles you recommend for Llama-2-13B variants at 512-token context for best latency/cost tradeoff?
- Any constraints on using prefix caching across sessions for our multi-tenant streams?

If you can send a short playbook + a sample Mutual Action Plan / SOW, procurement will move quickly.

Cheers,
Sam
Sam Lee
Head of ML Platforms, AtlasGrid
From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova>
Date: 2027-03-02T10:05:00-07:00
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@atlasgrid.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz, karthik_iyer
Subject: Re: Quick question on Optimize Toolkit pilot structure

Hi Sam — great to hear. Looping in Vanessa (Sales) and Karthik (Solutions/Inference) to scope the technical bits and a pilot commercial.

Quick answers while we pull the playbook:
- Pricing: we typically structure a 3-month pilot as a time-boxed committed capacity + usage credits. For 50M tokens/mo we propose a small committed throughput band + a one-time onboarding credit (we can front-load an efficiency workshop). I'll share a draft with numbers.
- Quant profiles: Karthik will suggest the specific quant/engine mix — generally 4-bit Q4 variants on A100/H100-like hardware for 13B give the best cost/latency balance; for aggressive cost targets we can recommend 3-bit variants with a short eval set to validate quality regression.
- Prefix/KV caching: supported — we recommend a session-local prefix cache strategy when you have strong session affinity; cross-tenant shared caches require pinned model instances and an elevated security review (we can include options in the SOW).

Sending a one-pager + pilot MAP by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Sofia
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer>
Date: 2027-03-02T11:40:00-07:00
To: sofia_ivanova, vanessa_ortiz
Subject: Re: Quick question on Optimize Toolkit pilot structure (tech notes)

Sofia / Vanessa — quick tech notes to include in the playbook for AtlasGrid's 512-token use case:

- Recommended runtime mix:
  * Default: q4_0 13B variant on Redwood Dedicated H100 pool — ~18-25% token-cost reduction vs fp16 with ~1–3% quality delta on summarization prompts.
  * If AtlasGrid is extremely cost-sensitive: q3_k_mixed for inference-critical paths; requires eval on their 5k prompt test-suite to surface failure modes.
- Batching guidance:
  * Continuous batching with dynamic batch sizing tuned to P95 latency target (we typically configure 4–6ms token addition budget for streaming workloads).
  * For 50M tokens/mo, enable autoregressive KV caching for warm prefixes to reduce duplicate computation by ~30% at steady state.
- Prefix caching recommendations:
  * Session-local caches by conversation ID: safe default, no additional compliance review.
  * Cross-session shared caches: requires per-account isolated instances or dedicated capacity (included in Dedicated pricing).
- Measurement & rollback hooks:
  * Quality tracking: run the AtlasGrid test-suite through our Eval runner daily during pilot; tie regressions >1.5% to automatic fallback to non-quantized model.

I'll attach a short quant benchmark CSV and a config snippet.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova>
Date: 2027-03-03T09:18:00-07:00
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@atlasgrid.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz, karthik_iyer, priyom_das
Subject: AtlasGrid Optimize Toolkit pilot proposal (3-month outline)

Sam — attaching a concise pilot proposal and a draft SOW (see attachments). High-level commercial offer below; open to fine-tuning.

Pilot summary (3 months):
- Scope: inference for document summarization, up to 50M tokens/month; evaluation of q4_0 vs q3 mixed quantized profiles; batching + KV caching enabled; quality guardrails + daily evals.
- Commercials:
  * Pilot package price: $28,000 flat pilot credit (applies to usage).
  * Committed throughput band: equivalent to 2 dedicated GPU slots for the pilot window to ensure stable P95 latency.
  * Optional: additional 10% onboarding credit if AtlasGrid signs a 12-month committed Dedicated contract within 30 days of pilot close.
- Success criteria:
  * Avg summarization latency <= 600ms per request at target load,
  * Cost per 1k tokens reduced by >= 25% vs current baseline,
  * Quality delta vs fp16 <= 2% on AtlasGrid test-suite.

Technical addenda:
- Quantization: recommend q4_0 as default; run a 2-week A/B eval against q3_k_mixed if they want max cost savings.
- Caching: session-local KV caching on shared instances; cross-account caching requires dedicated pools and additional security review (we note this in SOW).

Next steps:
1) If that works, procurement sends PO to procurement@atlasgrid.com referencing deal AG-2027-PILOT-47.
2) We run an onboarding week (workshop + eval set ingest).
3) Pilot kicks off with weekly checkpoints.

Attachments: AtlasGrid_SOW_v1.pdf, quantization-benchmarks.csv, pilot-MAP-template.docx

Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through.

Best,
Sofia
